findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Make `_schema_plan_review_findings` import `rebar.llm.plan_review.passes` (or call `passes.register_contracts()`) right before `contracts.response_model_for("plan_review_findings")`, and add a test that it validates against the Pass-1 model, not the review_result fallback.
evidence: contracts.py:38-40: `if output_schema and output_schema in _CONTRACTS: return _CONTRACTS[output_schema]()` / `return findings.findings_response_model()` — unknown names silently use the review_result model
passes.py:120-132: `register_contracts()` runs only as a side effect of importing `rebar.llm.plan_review.passes`
Plan: 'registered by importing `rebar.llm.plan_review.passes`, `passes.py:120`' — the scorer is not told to perform the import
findings.finding: The new scorer depends on `plan_review_findings` already being registered. If it isn't, `contracts.response_model_for` does not raise: it falls back to `findings.findings_response_model()`, the review_result model that requires `dimension`. The plan says only that the contract is 'registered by importing rebar.llm.plan_review.passes'. It does not require the scorer to do that import itself, so correctness depends on someone else having imported passes first.
scenarios: A unit test or offline re-score calls `score("emits_valid_findings", case, out)` on a hand-built Pass-1 output in a process where passes was never imported, and gets "'dimension' is a required property" again
A later refactor makes eval_solver import passes lazily or not at all, and the bug silently comes back
findings.suggested_fix: Inside `_schema_plan_review_findings`: `from rebar.llm.plan_review import passes; passes.register_contracts(); model = contracts.response_model_for("plan_review_findings")`. Optionally assert `"findings" in model.model_fields` and that the item model has a `finding` field, so a silent fallback fails loudly.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] In `_schema_plan_review_findings`, import `rebar.llm.plan_review.passes` inside the scorer (or call `passes.register_contracts()`), or build the model directly from `passes._pass1_model()`. If `plan_review_findings` is not registered, return a failed ScoreResult. Add a test that calls the scorer on a hand-built Pass-1 output without calling `run_case` first.
evidence: src/rebar/llm/contracts.py:38-40: `if output_schema and output_schema in _CONTRACTS: return _CONTRACTS[output_schema]()` / `return findings.findings_response_model()` — an unknown name silently falls back to the review_result model

eval_scorers.py imports nothing from plan_review at module top (the scorers import lazily inside function bodies), so registration depends on whatever was imported earlier

Plan text: "(registered by importing `rebar.llm.plan_review.passes`, `passes.py:120`)" says how registration works but does not require the scorer to import passes or to fail when the contract is missing
findings.finding: The new scorer gets its model from `contracts.response_model_for("plan_review_findings")`. For any name that is not registered, that function silently returns `findings.findings_response_model()`, which is the review_result model that requires `dimension`. If `eval_scorers` is loaded in a process that has not yet imported `rebar.llm.plan_review.passes`, the new scorer validates against the old schema and the same "'dimension' is a required property" error comes back. The plan says the contract is "registered by importing rebar.llm.plan_review.passes" but never requires the scorer to do that import, and never says what happens if the contract is missing.
scenarios: `rebar prompt eval` or `run_eval` scores a stored or replayed output without first running the solver, or a unit test calls `score("emits_valid_findings", ...)` directly on a hand-built output in a fresh interpreter. The contract is unregistered, the scorer validates against review_result, and a valid Pass-1 finding fails on `dimension`.
findings.suggested_fix: Inside `_schema_plan_review_findings`: `from rebar.llm.plan_review import passes  # registers plan_review_findings` before calling `contracts.response_model_for(...)`. Alternatively call `passes._pass1_model()` directly so the unregistered-name fallback can never be reached.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Give `emits_valid_findings` at least one check that real criterion-arm output can fail, e.g. every finding's `finding` text must be non-empty after strip, and add a `run_case`-driven test where the FakeRunner returns an empty `finding` and the scorer fails.
evidence: passes.py:289: `"finding": f.get("finding", "")` — the key is always present after normalization
passes.py:284-286: findings with no in-chunk criteria are dropped, so surviving `criteria` is never empty
passes.py:50: `finding: str` — the empty string validates
Plan Testing: 'a finding missing `finding` ... fail[s] emits_valid_findings' — this case cannot come out of `run_case`
findings.finding: Against real criterion-arm output, the new scorer can never fail. `pass1_chunk`/`pass1_container` rebuild every finding as `{"finding": f.get("finding", ""), "criteria": <non-empty in-set list>, ...}`, so `finding` is always present (possibly empty) and `criteria` is always a non-empty list. The P1Finding model only requires `finding: str`, which accepts `""`. The failure paths the plan tests (missing `finding`, non-list `findings`, non-dict) can only happen with hand-built outputs. An empty-text finding produced by the solver would pass.
scenarios: The model returns a finding with an empty or missing `finding` text; the solver fills in `""`, and `emits_valid_findings` still passes, so a degraded finder is never caught by the gating schema scorer

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State in the Approach that `emits_valid_findings` validates the solver's normalized Pass-1 output (after pass1_chunk/pass1_container coercion), and either accept that scope explicitly or also reject empty `finding` text so a coerced missing finding still fails.
evidence: src/rebar/llm/plan_review/passes.py:284-301 (pass1_chunk): `crit = [c for c in (f.get("criteria") or []) if c in ids]; if not crit: continue` then `"finding": f.get("finding", "")`, plus `_agentic` and `cohort` keys
passes.py:379-412 (pass1_container): the same coercion and drop, plus `_container_child` and `_container_bin`
eval_solver.py:138,150: `return {"findings": list(findings)}`, the normalized list that is passed to the scorers
P1Finding (passes.py:50) types `finding` as a plain `str`, so the coerced `""` validates
findings.finding: The scorer does not see the model's raw structured output. `pass1_chunk` and `pass1_container` rebuild every finding first. They coerce a missing `finding` to `""` (`f.get("finding", "")`), default missing lists to `[]`, and drop any finding whose `criteria` has no in-set id. They also add extra keys (`_agentic`, `cohort`, `_container_child`, `_container_bin`). As a result, the malformed cases the plan's ACs list ("missing `finding`", wrong criterion) can never reach the live scorer. Only the synthetic unit tests exercise them, and in the live loop the check reduces to "findings is a list". The plan never mentions this normalization step or says that the scorer validates normalized output, so it may overstate what `emits_valid_findings` checks live.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria bullet 2 ("Malformed plan-review output (missing `finding`, non-list `findings`, non-dict) still fails") / Testing failure path
scenarios: The model emits a finding with no `finding` text. pass1_chunk turns it into `finding: ""`, `emits_valid_findings` passes, and nobody notices a contract-violating output in the live eval.
